history.dynasty: Paramara-era (Gurjara-Chalukya style); renovation by Chaulukya king Siddharaj Jaysinh (Samvat 1198 per 1964 excavation records - verify)
history.period: Circa 10th-11th century AD (per architectural analysis); renovation dated Samvat 1198 (c. 1141-42 CE)
history.summary: The Bilpakeshwara Temple at Bilpank village, ~18 km southwest of Ratlam on the Mhow-Neemuch highway, is an ancient Shiva temple also called Virupaksha Mahadev. It is a Panchayatana temple - east-facing, Nirandhara Mulaprasada with Sapta-Ratha-Garbhagriha, comprising Garbhagriha, Antarala and Mahamandapa on one axis - built in Gurjara-Chalukyan style contemporary with the Paramara temple pattern. No direct inscription of its founding survives; on the basis of a 1964 excavation at Bilpank it is recorded that Chaulukya king Siddharaj Jaysinh of Gujarat renovated it in Samvat 1198. It is described (Drishti IAS, 2022) as the country's third Virupaksha temple; a temple development master plan (grand entrance, dharamshalas, yajnashala, parking, chemical-conservation treatment) was taken up for restoration in 2022. CSV town 'Ratlam' corrected: the temple is at Bilpank, Ratlam district.

name: Bilpakeshwara Temple
town: Bilpank (CSV town 'Ratlam' is the district headquarters; the temple is at Bilpank village, ~18 km southwest of Ratlam)
town_description: Bilpank is a village in Ratlam district, Madhya Pradesh, about 18 km southwest of Ratlam city on the Mhow-Neemuch highway. It is known almost entirely for the ancient Virupaksha (Bilpakeshwara) Mahadev Temple, an ASI-noted 10th-11th century Panchayatana shrine that draws devotees especially on Mahashivratri. The village sits in the Malwa agricultural belt; Ratlam city, a major railway junction, is the gateway for visitors.
